item.title: 2027: Sowore faults NELFUND, promises non-repayable grants
item.description: By Dickson Omobola African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore, Friday, faulted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), saying he will abolish the scheme if elected. Sowore promised to introduce N100,000 grants per semester for students, saying the scheme would provide financial support without requiring repayment. He made the promise during a live session on his Facebook page, adding that students should not be burdened with debt while pursuing their education. He said, “The NELFUND that this government has put in place. First, our party is going to abolish NELFUND. We will turn it into grants.” He added that the policy would replace the existing student loan arrangement. He said, “We are going to give N100,000 per semester, which is N20,000 more than what they are getting now. For two semesters, you get N200,000 so that you can focus on your studies.” Sowore argued that Nigeria should avoid introducing a system that could leave graduates struggling with debt, particularly in a country where employment opportunities were limited. Citing his experience in the United States, where he said he spent 20 years, the AAC candidate described student loans as a source of financial hardship for many graduates. He said, “The biggest cause of depression in America is student loans. Where are you going to get the employment to pay back the loans? But the truth is that even the loans they are giving to them now, they are not paying back. So it just makes sense to turn it into grants.” Sowore said a student completing a four-year program would receive a total of N400,000 under the proposed arrangement, assuming two semesters per year. He described the amount as a reasonable investment in young Nigerians who would contribute decades of service to the country. The former presidential candidate also proposed scholarships for students with outstanding academic abilities, saying beneficiaries could be sponsored to study abroad. “Grants for anybody, whether… scholarships for people who show exemplary ability. We give you a scholarship; we send you abroad,” he said. He advocated increased government investment in education, citing China’s support for students studying abroad as an example of how countries could develop their education systems. Sowore blamed the decline in Nigeria’s education sector for several of the country’s challenges, arguing that investment in schools was essential to reducing poverty and developing human capital. He recalled that during his childhood, free education and community efforts to ensure school attendance made education a priority. The activist also cited the University College Hospital, Ibadan, as an example of Nigeria’s former standing in the health sector, saying members of foreign royal families previously travelled to the country for medical treatment. item.title: Waste crisis: Acting LAWMA MD resumes, reads riot act to staff
item.description: .unveils 60-day action plan ​By Olasunkanmi Akoni Amid mounting concerns over waste management across the metropolis, the newly appointed Acting Managing Director of the Lagos Waste Management Authority, LAWMA, Olajuwon Akinyemi, has assumed office with a stern warning to the workforce, reading the riot act against laxity. Akinyemi, also unveiled a 60-day emergency action plan to clear backlogs and restore the agency’s past glory. ​Addressing management and staff at a tense workers’ forum held at LAWMA’s Ijora-Olopa headquarters on Friday, he made it clear that business as usual was over. Accompanied by the Acting Executive Director, Operations, Dr. Olorunwa Tijani, and the Executive Director, Finance, Mr. Kunle Adebiyi, the new helmsman demanded total commitment, positive work ethics, and renewed dedication to duty from every personnel, warning that repositioning the agency requires uncompromising discipline and active participation from all ranks. ​”We are bringing in resilience and a new paradigm shift. It is a new wave in handling waste in Lagos. “We already have the template to transform LAWMA positively. All we need to do is recreate, modernise and do better than in the past,” Akinyemi declared, signaling zero tolerance for operational inefficiencies. ​To back up his charge, Akinyemi rolled out a 60-day blueprint aimed at rapid waste evacuation, stricter regulatory enforcement, and aggressive field monitoring across Lagos State. While giving key highlights of the emergency plan, the MD boss said personnel will be redeployed across the state’s three operational districts based on their familiarity with local terrains to sharpen field monitoring and speed up response times. Hinting on decentralised operational hubs, Akinyemi added that the hubs will be established to decentralise waste management, tighten supervision, and bring rapid intervention closer to blackspots requiring urgent attention. On ​indiscriminate dumping, he avowed the agency’s determination to intensify community sensitization on waste sorting at source, mobilizing traditional rulers, Community Development Association (CDA) leaders, market associations, and artisans to enforce responsible disposal habits. item.title: I Would’ve Advised El-Rufai To Talk Less If I Had Had Contact With Him — Yahaya Bello
item.description: Former Kogi State Governor, Yahaya Bello, has said he would have advised former Kaduna State governor, Nasir El-Rufai, to speak less if he had had the opportunity to speak with him before his legal battle began. Bello, who spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday, said he would have urged El-Rufai to talk less, remain in the All Progressives Congress (APC) that he helped build, and wait to see what President Bola Tinubu would do. He described El-Rufai as a respected and idealistic person who pursues whatever he believes in. Bello said that though he does not wish him “to go down the drain,” the embattled former Kaduna governor must have learnt how to handle political differences. El-Rufai is facing legal battles involving the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) and the Department of State Services (DSS), alongside allegations of financial misconduct and unlawful phone interception. In October, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal against the refusal of bail in the alleged financial misconduct case, upholding his continued detention by the ICPC. In a separate DSS prosecution over alleged unlawful interception of National Security Adviser Nuhu Ribadu’s telephone communications, the Federal High Court on October 26 dismissed his no-case submission and ordered him to enter his defence, adjourning proceedings to November 25. The Kaduna corruption trial, involving an alleged ₦8.68 billion CCTV contract, was adjourned to December 8, while a ₦1 billion fundamental rights suit against the ICPC, police and AGF is scheduled for judgment on December 2. item.title: Oyedele urges banks to prioritise agricultural lending
item.description: …Commissions Moniepoint Abuja branch By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has urged banks and other financial institutions to make loans more affordable and accessible to businesses, particularly those operating in the agricultural sector, to stimulate productivity and economic growth. Oyedele made the call on Friday at the commissioning of the Abuja branch office of Moniepoint Microfinance Bank (MFB). He said access to affordable financing remained a major challenge for small businesses, stressing that interest rates, fees, repayment periods and the time required to secure loans must be considered in determining the usefulness of credit facilities. “We also must make business finance more affordable and more useful for many small businesses. The challenge is obtaining finance at a cost and on terms that they can sustain. “Affordability involves the interest rates, the fees that we charge, the repayment period, and time spent securing even that facility itself. All of these decide whether financing helps a business or puts it under strain,” he said. The minister said while the government had a responsibility to strengthen economic conditions to make financing more affordable, financial institutions must also contribute through efficient operations, improved risk assessment and transparent pricing. He particularly emphasised the need for increased lending to agriculture, noting that every segment of the value chain required adequate financial support. According to him, farmers need timely access to inputs and working capital, aggregators require funds to purchase produce, while processors need financing for equipment, storage and reliable supplies. He added that transporters and traders also required financial support to move agricultural products efficiently to consumers. Oyedele said appropriate financing for the sector would boost food production, reduce post-harvest losses, improve rural incomes and create employment opportunities. He, however, cautioned that agricultural lending must reflect the realities of farming, including production cycles, weather conditions and market risks. “Repayment schedules should follow production and harvest cycles. Lending decisions should recognise risks such as weather and market conditions, and partnerships with cooperatives, insurers, buyers and other credible participants can help lenders understand and manage them better,” he said. The minister urged Moniepoint to deepen its engagement with agricultural businesses and develop practical partnerships to support viable enterprises. On data protection, Oyedele called on financial institutions to strengthen safeguards around customers’ personal and financial information to protect them against fraud and other abuses. item.title: Tinubu focused on next generation, not next election, Owan-Enoh says
item.description: …Targets APC victory in all 18 Cross River LGAs By Ike Uchechukwu, Calabar The Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Owan-Enoh, has said President Bola Tinubu is focused on building a prosperous future for Nigerians rather than seeking victory at the next election. Owan-Enoh stated this on Friday at Ikom Township Stadium during the inauguration of the Cross River chapter of Project Beyond’s executive and polling unit structures for the Central and Northern Senatorial Districts of the state. He described Tinubu as a pragmatic leader whose decisions were driven by long-term national development rather than immediate political considerations. The minister likened the President’s leadership approach to that of Singapore’s founding Prime Minister, Lee Kuan Yew, whom he credited with transforming the Asian country into a global success story. “That Prime Minister didn’t look at politics the same way a politician looks at the next election. That Prime Minister looked at the next generation. “That is what President Bola Tinubu is doing,” he said. Owan-Enoh acknowledged that the President’s economic reforms had subjected many Nigerians to hardship but described the sacrifices as temporary measures necessary for economic recovery. He likened the reforms to bitter medicine that would eventually restore the country’s economic health. “That tablet is bitter. But after that bitterness, you’ll get well,” he said. According to him, Nigeria has begun experiencing economic recovery and stability after three and a half years of the administration’s policies. He said the government’s next priority was to translate the gains into prosperity and improved purchasing power for Nigerians. “Three and a half years later, recovery has started. Stability has set in, and I think for President Tinubu, the next concentration is prosperity. “The next concentration is the power of your pocket,” he said. The minister further claimed that inflation had declined to about 14 per cent, expressing optimism that it would continue to fall towards single digits. He urged Cross River residents to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the state needed to maintain its influence in national decision-making. “You will need to sit at the table when decisions are taken for you to be able to put before that table what you want,” he said. Owan-Enoh said securing the state’s political relevance required a strong electoral showing for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Recalling the 2023 presidential election, he said Tinubu won in seven of Cross River’s 18 local government areas. He, however, challenged party members to work towards securing victory in all 18 local government areas in the January 16, 2027 presidential election. “In 2023, out of 18 local governments, the President won seven. “In 2027, we must leave here with a determination and a resolve that, come January 16, 2027, Mr President is going to win 18 over 18 in Cross River, and that is possible,” he said. item.title: ‘I won’t disappoint you in my second term’ – Adeleke assures Osun people
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As the week-long activities to usher Governor Ademola Adeleke’s second term in office took off with Jumat service, the governor has vowed not to disappoint the people of the State. Represented by the Deputy Governor, Prince Kola Adewusi, at the Oja Oba Central mosque in Osogbo, the Governor recalled the struggles and battles for the sustenance of democracy in Osun State and vowed to continue to place the interest of the public at the heart of his administration. A statement issued by his spokesperson, Olawale Rasheed, on Friday stated that the governor commended Osun people for their steadfastness, perseverance and persistent solidarity during the electioneering period, saying the state has become a national model, a symbol for people’s power as the foundation of democracy. “I won’t disappoint Osun people. I will deliver even more than my first term. I am hopeful our financial situation will soon improve with the expected resolution of the local government crisis. We will take good care of workers and all segments of the society,” the governor was quoted as saying. Earlier in his sermon, Sheikh Moruf Ishola described the recent Osun election as “unprecedented in many respects and a standout record for all students of democracy. According to him, the Osun election that re-elected Governor Adeleke broke all records in terms of its dynamics and colours, adding that “the August 15 polls defied all calculations because almighty Allah ran it. “That is why Mr Governor must not abandon God and the people. He must continue to govern with the fear of God, keep promises and serve only the interests of the people,” he submitted on behalf of the Chief Imam of Osogboland, Sheikh Musa Animasahun. The prayer session was attended by the Secretary to the State Government, Hon. Teslim Igbalaye; Osun Central Accord Senatorial candidate, Hon. Ganiyu Olaoluwa; members of the state executive council; special advisers; and top government functionaries. item.title: UNICEF, Lagos raise alarm over threats to children’s rights
item.description: …As children demand free education, protection, greater say in policies By Chioma Obinna The United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and the Lagos State Government have called for stronger protection of children’s rights, warning that their welfare and fundamental rights are increasingly under threat and require concrete government action. The call was made on Friday during the commemoration of the 2026 World Children’s Day at the UNICEF Lagos Office, with the theme, “My Day. My Rights. My Future.” UNICEF Chief of Field Office, Lagos, Celine Lafoucriere, said children’s rights were facing growing threats globally, stressing the need for governments and other stakeholders to guarantee every child access to education, healthcare, good nutrition, clean water, sanitation and social protection. “Children’s rights are under pressure, they’re under threat, they’re being increasingly threatened throughout the world,” she said. Lafoucriere said UNICEF was working closely with the Lagos State Government to ensure that children’s rights were respected and accessible to all, particularly the most vulnerable. She emphasised the importance of social protection programmes, noting that the existence of rights did not automatically translate into access to basic necessities. “Having a right is one thing, but it’s not going to put food on the table,” she said, explaining that social protection interventions could help vulnerable children access education, healthcare and adequate nutrition. She added that Nigeria’s future depended largely on the attention and investment devoted to children today. “The child is the future, and the future of Nigeria is today,” Lafoucriere declared. The Lagos State Commissioner for Youth and Social Development, Mobolaji Ogunlende, said the government remained committed to promoting the welfare, protection and development of every child but acknowledged that it could not achieve the objective without the support of other stakeholders. He urged parents, schools, communities, development partners and other stakeholders to work together to create an environment where every child felt safe, valued and heard. “We must translate what we hear today into meaningful action and commitment,” he said. Ogunlende assured the children that their contributions and concerns raised during the celebration would not end with the event but would inform government policies and practical interventions. Also speaking, the Speaker of the Lagos State Children’s Parliament, Abdulsalam Anjola, called for greater involvement of children in decisions affecting their lives, insisting that their voices must be considered in the formulation of policies concerning them. He said children were better positioned to communicate their experiences, particularly in cases involving abuse and other challenges. item.title: Ooni urges FG to revive, protect textile industry
item.description: …Calls for prioritisation of Nigerian fabrics, investment in local production By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, has called on the Federal Government to revive and protect Nigeria’s textile industry as part of efforts to strengthen the nation’s economic growth and development. The monarch also urged textile unions to deploy all necessary measures to safeguard the industry and encourage the patronage of locally produced fabrics. Oba Ogunwusi, represented by Olori Aderonke Adeyeye, made the call on Friday at the 38th Annual National Education Conference of the National Union of Textile, Garment and Tailoring Workers of Nigeria (NUTGTWN) and the Nigeria Textile, Garment and Tailoring Employers’ Association in Ile-Ife, Osun State. Commending the unions for organising the conference to educate their members, the monarch said an informed labour union was essential to the survival of democracy and the development of the nation. He said stakeholders must work together to restore the country’s textile industry, revive moribund mills and make locally manufactured fabrics a source of national pride. “It is important for stakeholders to protect our industry. Let us prioritise our own fabrics. Let us revive our textile mills. Let us make Made in Nigeria a badge of pride, not an apology. “We must honour labour. Every tailor, every cutter, every employer deserves dignity, fair pay and respect. Labour is not servitude; labour is nation-building. “Let us raise a new generation. Teach them craft, teach them the business, teach them discipline. Do not let this knowledge die with us,” he said. The Ooni further stressed that the survival of democracy was closely linked to economic prosperity, respect for workers and the protection of local industries. “Democracy cannot stand on empty stomachs. It cannot stand where labour is not respected. It cannot stand where industry is allowed to die. A nation that abandons its artisans abandons its future,” he added. Earlier, NUTGTWN President, Comrade Peter Godonu, urged the Federal Government to translate its commitment to industrialisation into concrete policies and investments capable of reviving the country’s struggling textile industry. Godonu said Nigeria could no longer afford to celebrate the potential of its textile sector while factories remained closed, production capacity declined and imported products continued to dominate the domestic market. He said the union would sustain its advocacy for policies that promote industrialisation, local production, decent work and the revival of the textile and garment industry. “Our Union will therefore continue to intensify its advocacy and campaign for sustainable industrialisation, local production, decent work and the revival of the textile and garment industry. “We remain available to partner with the Federal Government, state governments, employers and other stakeholders in developing and implementing practical solutions to these challenges,” h

item.title: 2027: Court sacks ADC governorship candidate in Adamawa
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Friday ordered the removal of Tukur Ribadu as the 2027 Adamawa governorship candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC). Justice Obiora Egwuatu, in a judgment, held that Mr Omar Suleiman, who won the majority of the valid votes cast in the primary election of the party, was unlawfully substituted by Ribadu. Justice Egwuatu ordered the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to immediately restore Suleiman as the rightful candidate of the party. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Suleiman, a cousin of former Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Babachir Lawal, was said to have initially emerged as the ADC’s candidate in the Adamawa primary. However, he was later replaced by Ribadu. Dissatisfied, Suleiman filed a suit marked FHC/ABJ/C’S/1751/2026 before Justice Egwuatu to challenge his unlawful substitution. He prayed the court to order the ADC to forward his name to the electoral umpire as a valid candidate of the party. He also prayed the court to compel INEC to publish his name as the candidate of the party. Delivering the judgment, Justice Egwuatu held that Suleiman could only be replaced as a candidate if he had formally and voluntarily withdrawn from the race or died. He ruled that since Suleiman had neither withdrawn nor died, his replacement was illegal, null and void. The judge consequently ordered INEC to immediately restore his name as the ADC governorship candidate for Adamawa State in the forthcoming governorship poll. item.title: Vandalism, illegal connections threaten Kano water supply
item.description: Over 45 pipeline repairs completed, says commissioner By Hadiza Yusuf KANO — The Kano State Government has warned residents against vandalism, illegal connections and other activities capable of damaging public water infrastructure and disrupting the supply of drinking water across the state. The Commissioner for Water Resources, Dr Dahiru Muhammad Hashim, gave the warning at a press conference in Kano on Friday while briefing journalists on the progress of ongoing rehabilitation of water facilities and restoration of supply to communities. Hashim said the ministry had identified cases of unauthorised connections to water pipelines, vandalism, indiscriminate drilling around major water lines and improper handling of distribution valves. He added that some water pipes had also been damaged by construction activities, refuse burning and other activities around drainage channels. “We appeal to the general public to cooperate with the Ministry in protecting water infrastructure. Our assessment has identified cases of unauthorised tapping of pipelines, vandalism and damage to pipes crossing drainage channels,” he said. The commissioner urged residents, contractors and those executing construction, road and drainage projects to consult relevant authorities before embarking on activities that could affect water pipelines. He also called on residents to promptly report burst pipes, leakages, suspected vandalism and illegal connections to the appropriate authorities. According to him, the restoration of water supply has exposed weaknesses in some old pipelines, many of which had remained without regular water flow for several years. He explained that the return of water pressure to the distribution network had resulted in leakages and pipe bursts in some locations, necessitating urgent repairs and replacement of damaged infrastructure. Hashim disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 45 repair and replacement interventions across different parts of the metropolis. The affected areas include Goron Dutse, Jakara, Kofar Ruwa, Kurmi, Dukawa, Kofar Wambai, Fagge, Club Road, Tudun Wada, Gidan Zakka, Gabari, Koki, Mandawari and Sharada. He said the interventions involved replacing damaged asbestos-cement pipes, fixing leaking PVC pipelines, installing valves and repairing faulty connections. The commissioner further disclosed that water had been pumped from Challawa Water Works to the Goron Dutse reservoirs, which have a reported capacity of 42.5 million litres, before being released into the distribution network. He listed communities that had received water to include Goron Dutse, Gwammaja, Jakara, Kofar Mazugal, Muskwani, Kofar Wambai, Mandawari, Fagge, Tudun Wada, Gama, Kofar Ruwa and Alfindiki, among others. item.title: Tinubu Must Stay group set to unveil presidential library, reform observatory
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Tinubu Movement for Sustainable Governance Foundation TMS, popularly known as Tinubu Must Stay, has announced plans to establish a National Reform Documentation and Impact Observatory, a public digital policy archive and a possible future presidential library for President Bola Tinubu. Chairman of the Board of Trustees and National Coordinator of the group, Malam Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, disclosed this on Friday during the commissioning of its National Secretariat in Abuja. He said the records would start with Tinubu’s years as Governor of Lagos State between 1999 and 2007, then cover policy developments under successive administrations, his national political career and his presidency from 2023. According to him, the archive would span public revenue administration, infrastructure, investment, education, economic management, digital transformation and institutional development. Students, researchers, historians, policymakers and ordinary citizens would be given access to original documents, implementation records, economic data and independent assessments. Inuwa said the library, the observatory and the archive remained long-term aspirations that would need feasibility studies, sustainable funding, proper governance and professional archival standards. “History serves future generations when it preserves evidence, not merely admiration,” he said. He added that the documentation must make room for achievements, implementation difficulties, independent criticism and lessons learned. The announcement came with a membership claim. Inuwa said the group, formally launched on October 1, 2026, had recorded 61,093 validated members within seven weeks across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). He said the group had representation in 730 of the country’s 774 local government areas, about 94 per cent geographical coverage. Its digital database also captures 4,750 wards and 22,584 polling units. Inuwa said 65 per cent of members, roughly 40,000 people, were aged between 18 and 34, while the membership was 65 per cent men and 35 per cent women. “The most remarkable feature of our membership is its youthful composition. This is not merely a demographic statistic. It places a profound responsibility upon our institution,” he said. He said young Nigerians needed more than a seat in political conversations, naming quality education, employable skills, technology, finance and markets as what would turn the country’s demographic potential into prosperity. To that end, the group would run grassroots entrepreneurship workshops, digital skills training, mentorship programmes and policy dialogues. “Today, we are not merely opening an office. We are opening a new chapter in our responsibility to Nigeria,” he said. Inuwa said the secretariat would serve as a centre for research, civic engagement, youth empowerment and the documentation of policies and institutions shaping national development. item.title: Trump urges Nvidia to give Jensen Huang ‘second chance’
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Friday called for chip giant Nvidia to reinstate disgraced former CEO Jensen Huang after he resigned over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. “I would love to see him be back. You have one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world, and where is he going to go?” Trump told reporters. “I think that I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance.” Huang resigned last week as chief of Nvidia, a company at the center of the AI revolution, after revelations of an affair with an alleged Chinese spy who may have funneled restricted chips to that country. Reports of at least two further affairs emerged after that initial report, with US intelligence said to be aware of the possibility of the alleged Chinese espionage. Trump defended Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions.” “I’d like to see Jensen make a big apology and go back because he created something with Blackwell,” he said, referring to the most advanced chips designed by Nvidia. The US president also appeared to directly contradict his own treasury secretary, saying he had spoken to China’s President Xi Jinping about Huang during a summit earlier this week. “I did discuss that with President Xi, and he said, ‘Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He’s a brilliant man,'” said Trump. Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Trump had not discussed Huang with Xi during the meeting in Shenzhen. Trump advocated for Nvidia to take back Huang as their CEO “if they were smart.” Huang has offered to return to the company, a move the chip giant’s board has rejected. Board chair Harvey Jones said in an earnings call this week that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” – ‘Must stay ahead’ – Earlier, Bessent had spoken at length about the AI race with China in comments to US broadcaster CNBC. Speaking about the Trump administration’s support for the domestic AI sector, Bessent stressed that the United States “must stay ahead” of China in that realm. “Our best protection against the foreign SI and exploits by foreign actors is for our labs to maintain their substantial lead, and in effect, they are our shield against SI,” he said, using the government’s preferred SI, or “super intelligence.” “There’s no turning back on this. What we have to do is make sure that our labs maintain their leads through their continued innovation, through their access to the best chips, and through smart policy.” Bessent said Trump and Xi had agreed on certain guardrails on the use of AI in the military domain. “President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions,” he said. item.title: Nasarawa attracts $2.3bn investments in seven years — Abdullahi
item.description: Records 21 reforms, 11 PPP projects worth ₦93bn By John Alechenu ABUJA — Nasarawa State has attracted more than $2.3 billion in investments over the past seven years following reforms and institutional development aimed at making the state more competitive and investor-friendly. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nasarawa Investment and Development Agency, Ibrahim Abdullahi, disclosed this at the 13th World Public Relations Forum 2026 in Abuja. Abdullahi said the investments cut across agriculture, solid minerals, retail, commercial activities, manufacturing, agro-processing and education. He added that the state also implemented 11 public-private partnership (PPP) projects valued at about ₦93 billion within the period. According to him, the achievements were the outcome of seven years of reforms and deliberate institution-building under Governor Abdullahi Sule, rather than publicity campaigns or political slogans. Recounting the beginning of the process, Abdullahi said he was invited into the Nasarawa State public service seven years ago, when Governor Sule appointed him as economic adviser. He said the assignment was to develop the state’s investment profile and position it as an attractive destination for investors. He thanked the organisers of the forum for recognising Governor Sule with an honour presented a few days earlier. Abdullahi said one of the first lessons from the assignment was the need to establish the necessary structures before embarking on investment promotion. “So we could not go out and invite people to come to Nasarawa State without building any framework around it. That is to say that you cannot communicate something that is not there. You cannot communicate something that hasn’t been built. So, we put our heads down and began to build,” he said. He explained that the state’s vision, as contained in the Nasarawa Economic Development Strategy, was to make it one of Nigeria’s most competitive states through improved and accelerated economic growth that would translate into better living conditions for residents. Under the strategy, he said, the government implemented more than 21 reforms focused on improving the business environment and making the state attractive to investors. He said the reforms were designed to guarantee a conducive business climate, competitive returns on investment and improved general welfare for residents. According to him, the measures included the digitisation of revenue administration and improvements in the state’s fiscal and financial management framework. Abdullahi said the reforms provided the foundation for the state to confidently promote its investment opportunities to local and international investors. He noted that investors were attracted not by impressive speeches but by predictability, transparency, good returns and a government that honoured its commitments. item.title: The Other Black Gold: Nigeria’s Coffee Sector Wants A Shot
item.description: Richard Ali grew up with the aroma of coffee wafting through his house in central Nigeria as his father, an accountant, worked late into the night, drinking powdered, instant stuff from Maxwell House and Nescafé. It was not until years later, travelling on the other side of the continent, that Ali had a taste of “coffee, coffee — brewed coffee”. “I have to bring this to Nigeria,” he thought, and he started looking into importing beans from Rwanda. Ali later discovered he did not have to: coffee has been growing in Nigeria for more than 100 years. A wave of entrepreneurs in Africa’s most populous country are turning towards the oil-producing nation’s other black gold — an uphill task in a place full of tea and instant coffee, and little sense of homegrown java as a daily staple or part of a wider cultural patrimony. A general view of someone handling coffee beans in a plantation in the Gorongosa mountain range in Gorongosa on May 20, 2022. (Photo by Alfredo Zuniga / AFP) But roasters say they have found a market — and sense of national pride — to tap into, even if Nigeria’s beans are not well-known. “We need to grow more coffee, whether for the domestic market, which is expanding, or the global market, which is now considering Nigerian coffee,” Ali, founder of Tigray Coffee, which launched in 2021, said over a cup of Nigerian brew, light with slightly chocolatey notes. Agricultural Investments In Ethiopia, hundreds of years of cultivation have bound coffee to local culture, while Uganda and Ivory Coast have become modern export powerhouses. Nigeria produced 1,808 tonnes of beans in 2024, according to statistics from the UN’s Food and Agriculture Organisation — a paltry sum compared to Kenya’s 49,500 tonnes that same year. The first seeds hit the ground in Nigeria in the 19th century, after coffee was introduced by British colonists. The crop is notoriously fickle and can only grow in certain parts of the country. But there has also been a dearth of investment in agriculture, critics say, as the government instead became over-reliant on the oil sector for revenues. Experts have long called for a more diversified economy. The government agrees, at least in principle: in May, agriculture minister Abubakar Kyari announced federal investments in coffee production in Ondo State, calling it “a powerful economic crop” that could create jobs and “boost rural livelihoods”. ‘Never Imported Coffee’ At the opening of a new cafe in Lagos last month, Princess Adeyinka Tekenah paired a local brew not with croissants, but puff-puff, a staple street food snack of fried dough. “I have been in the business for 12 years, and I have never imported coffee,” the founder of Happy Coffee said. While Tekenah has leaned into her local roots, the coffee industry has also been helped by a growing sense of cosmopolitanism in Nigeria’s cities, Ali said.
